docs.text:
# DNS Resolution Failures

## Troubleshooting Flowchart

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Cannot Resolve Domain Names] --> B{Can ping IP addresses?}
    B -->|Yes| C[DNS Issue]
    B -->|No| D[General connectivity problem]
    C --> E[ipconfig /flushdns]
    E --> F[ipconfig /registerdns]
    F --> G[Change DNS to 8.8.8.8]
    G --> H[Restart DNS Client service]
    H --> I{Resolved?}
    I -->|Yes| J[Done]
    I -->|No| K[Run Network Troubleshooter]
    D --> L[See No Internet Guide]
    J --> M[Document]
    K --> M

docs.text:
# Connected to Wi-Fi but No Internet

## Troubleshooting Flowchart

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Connected but No Internet] --> B{Can other devices browse?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Local device issue]
    B -->|No| D[Router / ISP issue]
    C --> E[ipconfig /release → /renew]
    E --> F[ipconfig /flushdns]
    F --> G[Change DNS to 8.8.8.8]
    G --> H{Restarts services?}
    H -->|Yes| I[Problem Solved]
    H -->|No| J[Reset Winsock & IP stack]
    D --> K[Restart router\nContact ISP]
    I --> L[Document resolution]
    J --> L
    K --> L

# VPN Connection Problems

## Troubleshooting Flowchart

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[VPN Connection Issue] --> B{Internet works without VPN?}
    B -->|No| C[Fix base internet first]
    B -->|Yes| D[Restart VPN client & device]
    D --> E[Update VPN software]
    E --> F[Try different server]
    F --> G[Disable firewall/antivirus temporarily]
    G --> H{Connects?}
    H -->|Yes| I[Document]
    H -->|No| J[Check error code\nReset network stack]
    C --> K[See No Internet Guide]

Tip: Always start with basic questions: - When did the problem start? - Any recent changes (updates, new software, hardware)? - Error messages?

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• User reports "The password is incorrect"
  • Account locked after multiple failed attempts
  • User cannot log into domain-joined computer

docs.title: Quick L1 Resolution Steps
docs.text:
1. Log into a Domain Controller or machine with RSAT tools installed
  2. Open Active Directory Users and Computers (dsa.msc)
  3. Search for the user account
  4. Right-click the user → Reset Password
  5. Set a strong temporary password
  6. Check the box User must change password at next logon
  7. If locked: Right-click → Unlock Account

docs.title: Advanced Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Verify the account is not disabled
  • Check Account is sensitive and cannot be delegated (if applicable)
  • Run gpupdate /force on client after reset

docs.title: Related Articles
docs.text:
• Account Lockout Policy
  • Login Issues After Password Change

Prevention: Enable Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) in Microsoft Entra ID / Azure AD.

docs.title: Common Symptoms
docs.text:
• Sudden blue screen with stop code (e.g., IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL, CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED)
  • Computer restarts automatically

docs.title: L1 Troubleshooting Steps
docs.text:
1. Note the Stop Code and QR code on the BSOD
  2. Boot into Safe Mode (see Safe Mode guide)
  3. Open Event Viewer → Windows Logs → System
  4. Look for Critical/Error events around the crash time
  5. Run Memory Diagnostic Tool (mdsched.exe)
  6. Update drivers via Device Manager or Windows Update
  7. Check disk health: chkdsk C: /f /r

docs.title: Common Causes & Fixes
docs.text:
• Faulty RAM → Run Windows Memory Diagnostic
  • Driver issues → Update graphics/driver
  • Disk errors → Run chkdsk
  • Corrupted system files → sfc /scannow then DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth

docs.title: When to Escalate
docs.text:
• Crash persists after basic fixes
  • Multiple different stop codes

docs.text: ```markdown

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• User cannot log in (temporary profile loads)
  • Desktop looks default / missing files

docs.title: Fix Steps
docs.text:
1. Log in with another admin account
  2. Create a new local user account with admin rights
  3. Copy files from old profile (C:\Users\OldUsername) to new profile
  4. Remove old corrupted profile via Registry (advanced)
  5. Or use System Restore / repair install

docs.title: How to Boot into Safe Mode
Methods
docs.text:
Method 1: From Login Screen - Hold Shift while clicking Restart

Method 2: From Settings - Settings → Recovery → Advanced startup → Restart now

Method 3: Command Prompt (Admin) 

shutdown /r /o /f /t 00
In Safe Mode:

Limited drivers and services run Great for removing bad drivers, malware, or corrupted files

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Computer takes long to boot
  • Programs open slowly
  • High CPU/Disk usage

docs.title: Step-by-Step Troubleshooting
docs.text:
1. Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc)
  2. Sort by CPU / Memory / Disk usage
  3. Disable unnecessary startup programs (msconfig → Startup tab)
  4. Run Disk Cleanup + Storage Sense
  5. Check for malware (Windows Defender full scan)
  6. Update Windows and drivers
  7. Check disk health (chkdsk)
  8. Adjust Visual Effects (System Properties → Advanced → Performance Settings)

docs.title: Common Fixes
docs.text:
• Too many browser tabs / extensions
  • Low free disk space (<15%)
  • Fragmented HDD (defrag if applicable)

docs.title: Common Problems
docs.text:
• Updates fail to install
  • "Windows Update encountered an unknown error"
  • Stuck on downloading

docs.title: Troubleshooting Steps
docs.text:
1. Run Windows Update Troubleshooter
  2. Restart Windows Update service: 
    net stop wuauserv
net stop cryptSvc
net stop bits
net stop msiserver
ren C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution SoftwareDistribution.old
net start wuauserv
  3. Run sfc /scannow and DISM commands
  4. Manually download update from Microsoft Update Catalog
  5. Check disk space and internet connection
